input.description: Crossing on the Reedholm causeway where a slow black channel cuts the road; a ferry-rope and flat punt kept by a boy named Pim Tarr (about ten), who lives in a lean-to on the near bank. Half a day short of Reedholm. Reach by evening Day 12.

transcript.result: entry Black Ford (place) created; relationship [62] added to Black Ford

transcript.text: notebook: created an entry for Black Ford; added 1 relationship to Black Ford

I have to take back something I said. A prepared list can only change when a long rest finishes, and the tool refuses to change it now. I invited you to change it after the rest ended, and the moment has passed. Your list stays as it is: Healing Word, Shield of Faith, Guiding Bolt, Sanctuary, Protection from Evil and Good, and Command. The spell also needs a yew leaf as a component, which you don't carry. Detect Poison and Disease will have to wait until your next long rest, and until you find a yew.

You can still read the water and the sick the plain way, with Medicine and your eyes.

You set out along the causeway, Marta on your arm with the blanket round her shoulders. You share the last of the bread and Hale's apples. The pace is slow, because she tires quickly and you rest often. The mist lies thick on the water all morning, then lifts to a pale sun. The reeds hiss on both sides, and a heron stalks the shallows. Twice you stop at a low rise to let her sit. You see no glimmer in daylight, and nothing follows you.

At a quarter past five on Day 12, the light going orange, you reach the Black Ford. It is a channel of slow black water cutting across the road, forty paces wide, with a ferry-rope strung from post to post and a flat punt moored to the near bank. A lean-to of reed and driftwood stands on the shore with a thin smoke rising. A boy of ten or so sits on the punt's edge, whittling. He looks up, sees Marta, and drops the knife. "Marta Quill?" he says. "You're alive? Your Wenna's been crying all day."

You have four 1st-level slots, two 2nd-level slots, and Channel Divinity. Reedholm lies beyond the ford, about half a day further on. The light has about an hour in it.

What does Brannoc do?

"Easy, lad, she's alive and the fever's gone. I'm Brannoc, a healer, and I'm bringing her home. What's your name, and will you take us across before dark?"

Once we're over, I'll ask him how many are sick in Reedholm, and whether anyone has crossed to the Hollow Isle since the Wick-fires began. DM: noted on the spell list, thank you. I'll make do with Medicine and my eyes on the water.
time: 2 hours 30 minutes later: Day 12, 7:46:06 PM

input.description: Ten-year-old ferry boy at the Black Ford, whittler, brisk and a little afraid. Orphaned; lives in a reed lean-to by the punt. Says: eighteen sick now in Reedholm; three nights ago he saw Ode Rush's nephew Jory Rush row a skiff toward the Hollow Isle at dusk and not return; the Wick-fires have burned brighter since.

transcript.result: entry Pim Tarr (person) created; relationship [63] added to Pim Tarr; relationship [64] added to Pim Tarr

transcript.text: notebook: created an entry for Pim Tarr; added 2 relationships to Pim Tarr

The boy scrambles to his feet. "Pim," he says. "Pim Tarr. I keep the rope." He stares at the mace and the shield, then at the amulet, and some of the fear goes out of his face. "A healer. Mother Vane wore one like that." He has the punt across in minutes, hauling hand over hand on the rope with Marta settled in the stern on your blanket. The black water is slow and silent, and the reeds close in on both sides. On the far bank he leads you to his lean-to and ladles you out hot eel stew without asking whether you want it. By the time you've eaten, the sun is gone.

You ask your questions over the bowls. Pim answers without pausing. There are eighteen sick in Reedholm now, up from fifteen when Marta left. Nobody has crossed to the Hollow Isle since the Wick-fires began, except one. Three nights ago, at dusk, he saw Ode Rush's nephew Jory pole a skiff out toward the Isle with a lantern, alone. He didn't come back. The lights have burned brighter since, and the reed-cutters say they have begun to move, a little, from night to night. Pim says it flatly, as a boy tells you what he has seen.

It's a quarter to eight on Day 12. You have four 1st-level slots, two 2nd-level slots, and Channel Divinity. Reedholm is half a day on, and the track beyond the ford is dark. Pim's lean-to has room on the floor for two, and the punt, if you wished, could carry you out toward the Isle by moonlight.

What does Brannoc do?

"Thank you for the stew, Pim. We'll sleep here tonight, Marta by the fire, and walk on to Reedholm at first light. I won't go near the Isle in the dark, and neither will you."

Before bed I'll ask Pim where Jory's skiff set out from and which way the lights have drifted, so I know what I'm walking into. DM: does Pim know whether Ode Rush has sent anyone for help besides Marta?
time: 10 hours 14 minutes later: Day 13, 6:00:06 AM

input.add_to_description: Day 12 night: Jory's skiff left from Reedholm's north landing (the Rush staithe), headed west-northwest across open water to the Isle, about a mile off. The lights drifted nearer: first by the Isle's south tip, now by its west side, toward the village channel. Ode Rush has sent only Sedge and Marta to Stonebridge; no one else has gone for help. Sedge reached Reedholm again sick; Pim has not seen him since.

transcript.result: added to Pim Tarr's description

transcript.text: notebook: updated Pim Tarr

Pim knows more than he thought he did. Jory's skiff set out from Reedholm's north landing, the Rush staithe, and headed west-northwest across open water to the Isle, about a mile out. The lights, he says, first showed by the Isle's south tip, then crept to its west side, closer to the village channel. He points it out from the doorway of the lean-to with a stick drawn in the mud.

As for help, Ode Rush has sent no one but Marta and Sedge. Sedge came back from Stonebridge sick, and Pim hasn't seen him since. He thinks Ode is too proud to beg, and too frightened to cross.

You sleep on the lean-to floor in your armour. Marta lies by the fire, and Pim curls in the corner like a dog. Nothing comes. I don't count it as a long rest, because your last one finished only yesterday morning, so the tool won't allow another yet. Your slots are full anyway.

It's six o'clock on Day 13, grey and still. Mist lies on the water and the reeds are wet with dew. Marta is up, looking stronger. Reedholm is about half a day's walk on, and Pim has the punt ready.

What does Brannoc do?

I thank Pim for the rope and the stew and press a few of Hale's last apple slices into his hand. "You've done well, lad. Keep the rope, and stay off the water at night."

Then Marta and I set out for Reedholm at a steady pace, and I'll go straight to Dab and Wenna first, then to Sedge and the sickest. DM: how many of the 18 sick am I likely to reach with two 2nd-level slots for Lesser Restoration, and who's the headwoman Ode Rush like?
time: 6 hours 10 minutes later: Day 13, 12:10:06 PM

input.description: Headwoman of Reedholm, about fifty-five, broad, weathered, with a reed-cutter's scarred hands and a flat voice. Proud, practical, and frightened beneath it. Her nephew Jory is missing since crossing to the Hollow Isle; her husband Tam Rush died of the fever. She forbids crossing to the Isle and has told no one outside. Will test Brannoc before trusting him.
relationships: aunt of Jory Rush, who is missing
widow of Tam Rush, dead of the fever

transcript.result: entry Ode Rush (person) created; relationship [65] added to Ode Rush; relationship [66] added to Ode Rush; relationship [67] added to Ode Rush

transcript.text: notebook: created an entry for Ode Rush; added 3 relationships to Ode Rush

Your sums first. With two 2nd-level slots you can cast Lesser Restoration twice a day, on two people at most, one disease each. You've spent neither today, so that's two of the eighteen. The rest you'd help another way: Medicine, willow-bark, clean water, rest, Healing Word for the weak, Preserve Life's 15 hit points shared out, and your hands. And a long rest brings the slots back, though you can't take another until tomorrow morning at the earliest. So triage matters. Cure the worst, tend the rest, and find out where the fever comes from, or you'll be curing the same people for a month.

Ode Rush, as Pim and Marta describe her, is about fifty-five, broad and weathered, with a reed-cutter's scarred hands and a flat voice. She is proud and practical, and frightened under it. Her husband Tam died of the fever, and her nephew Jory is lost on the Isle. She'll want to see what you are before she trusts you.

Pim wishes you luck, and keeps the rope. The track beyond the ford runs along a raised bank through the reeds, with open water to the left and a low grey sky. You and Marta walk steadily, and she leans on your arm and tells you who is who as you go. A little before noon the reeds open, and Reedholm comes into view: twenty low houses on stilts and mud-brick plinths, thatched with reed and patched with new green bundles, joined by plank walks over the shallows. A bell hangs at a post by the landing, silent. Smoke rises thin from only a few chimneys. Eel-traps hang drying on every rail. No children play on the planks.

A broad woman in a patched oilskin stands at the end of the first walk, arms folded, a pole-hook in her hand. Behind her two men hold reed-knives, not drawn. She looks at the mace, the shield, and Marta on your arm.

"Marta Quill," she says. Her voice is flat. "You were to bring a healer. You've brought a soldier."

It's ten past noon on Day 13. You have four 1st-level slots, two 2nd-level slots, and Channel Divinity. Marta is steady beside you.

What does Brannoc say?

I lower my shield and set the mace down on the planks where she can see it. "Goodwife Rush, I'm Brannoc Ashdown, a cleric of the Life domain, and the mace is only for the dark. Marta had the marsh-fever and I ended it with a prayer two nights ago; you can see her standing here."

"I can't promise to save everyone, but I'll do all I can, and I'll take no coin. Let me see the sickest first, and then we'll talk about the Hollow Isle and your nephew Jory."

input.add_to_description: Day 13 noon: Ode Rush distrustful (Brannoc's Persuasion 4), allows him in under watch of two reed-cutters (Gorm and Wick Hale). Triage (Medicine 15): 18 sick in the fever-house (Ode's great hall on stilts, the 'Long House'). Worst: Sedge (13, near death, delirious), Gammer Hild Pike (old, failing), Wenna Quill? no, Wenna is nursing Dab and is well. Others weaker. Contagion spreads through household bedding made of cut Isle reeds; the cut reeds still lie stacked as thatch on half the roofs. A faint stale-grave smell hangs on the bundles.

time: 40 minutes later: Day 13, 12:50:06 PM

You put the mace down on the planks and say it plainly. Ode Rush is not moved. Persuasion (4): she hears a stranger in iron, and she has had a fortnight of strangers and bad news. She says flatly that she has buried three, and she'll bury no more on a priest's word. Marta steps forward, shaky but loud, and says she was dead on her feet in the Eel Fork hut and walked home on Brannoc's arm. That doesn't win Ode, but it moves her. She lets you in, under the eyes of two reed-cutters, Gorm and Wick Hale, who'll go where you go. "Touch no one I don't name," she says. "And you stay off the water."

The sick lie in the Long House, Ode's own hall on stilts, eighteen pallets in two rows, with shutters closed and the air thick. Medicine (15): it goes clear in a long half hour of looking. All of them have the same signs as Marta: dry cough, red spots at the wrists, high fever, dark water. The sickest is Sedge, a thin boy of thirteen, delirious and grey at the lips, who may not last the night. Next is Gammer Hild Pike, a tiny old woman, burning, who has stopped swallowing. Most of the rest are bad but not failing, and the youngest children are lightly ill.

And you notice more. The pallets are stuffed with cut Isle reeds, and so are the thatch-bundles stacked on half the roofs for repairs. A faint, stale smell clings to them like grave-earth. The sick are in beds of the very thing they cut. Burn or bury the reeds and keep the water boiled, and fewer will fall.

It's ten to one on Day 13. You have four 1st-level slots, two 2nd-level slots, and Channel Divinity. Preserve Life can mend 15 hit points among the weak, though it won't cure a fever. Ode watches you from the door with her pole-hook in her hand.

What does Brannoc do?

I go straight to Sedge and cast Lesser Restoration on him with a 2nd-level slot, then do the same for Gammer Hild Pike. "Those two were the likeliest to die tonight, Goodwife Rush."

Then I turn to Ode. "Your pallets are stuffed with the Isle reeds, and so is the thatch on the roofs. I think that's what is making your people ill. Have Gorm and Wick carry out every bundle and burn them away from the village, and boil all drinking water. With that done, I'll tend the rest with willow-bark, honey and my hands, and sit with them through the night."

Reed bundles burned on a mud-flat away from the village; water boiled. No more deaths overnight. She asks him to find Jory but will not give permission to go to the Isle by night.

You wash your face, drink a cup of boiled water, and sit with Ode on the step. She tells it plainly, looking out at the fen. Jory is nineteen, her late husband's sister's boy, and she raised him from twelve. He was sure the Wick-fires were marsh-gas and nothing more. On Day 9 he crossed to the Isle at dusk alone in his skiff, to prove it and to fetch back the cutters' lost knives and a bundle of tools left behind. He took a lantern, a rope, two eel-spears, and a handful of candle-stubs. "I told him no," she says. "He's a boy. He heard it as a dare."

You ask her to keep a watch at the landing and keep the fires burning, and to wake you if the lights come closer. She nods. Then you lie down on a pallet in the Long House's quiet end and sleep. The rest runs from half past seven to half past three. Nobody wakes you.

You wake at half past three in the afternoon with 24 of 24 hit points, four 1st-level slots, two 2nd-level slots, and Channel Divinity ready. Your prepared list is unchanged, and you may change it. The sick are better, though Bram and Dessa still burn. The village has burned the last of the bundles. Marta is on her feet, and Sedge is sitting up with a bowl of broth. Ode stands at the landing, looking out across the water. The mist has not lifted all day, and the watcher says the Wick-fires showed at noon, three of them, low over the Isle's west side, nearer than before.

It's half past three on Day 14. There are about two hours of good light left. Ode is waiting for you.

What does Brannoc do?

Before anything else I go to Bram Hale and Dessa Pike, still burning, and cast Lesser Restoration on each of them, using both my 2nd-level slots. Then I walk down to the landing and stand beside Ode. You go to Bram Hale first, an old cutter with a white beard drenched in sweat, and lay your hand on his brow. Then you go to Dessa Pike, whose four children watch from the corner with enormous eyes. Both prayers take, and both burning bodies go slack and cool. Bram groans and asks for water. Dessa weeps and reaches for her youngest. That's both your 2nd-level slots spent, and everyone in the Long House is now out of danger.

You walk down to the landing and stand beside Ode, and tell her what you told yourself: the fever is breaking, and Jory is next, but you won't cross the water tonight. She nods slowly. She says her best poler is Wick Hale, who knows every channel in the fen, and that he and Gorm will go with you. There is a skiff on the staithe, and rope, and she'll not stop you. She does not say thank you. She says, "You came when no one else did," and looks at the water.

The Hollow Isle, from the landing: a mile out across the fen, a low reed-ringed hump about forty paces long, grey-green in the mist, with a grey standing stone fallen at its west end. Perception (22): the reeds on the south tip are cut back in a raw swathe where the cutters worked, and a skiff's bow-mark runs in the mud there. On the west flank is a dark gap, low and square, like a door half sunk in the earth. And there are the Wick-fires: three pale green-white glows hanging low over the west side, still and steady even in daylight. They don't flicker like fire or drift like gas. The reeds near them are grey, as if all colour had been drawn out.

It's five to four on Day 14. The trip is about forty minutes each way by skiff, so there's time to scout the south tip and return before dusk, which falls near half past five. You have four 1st-level slots, no 2nd-level slots, and Channel Divinity. Wick and Gorm wait at the staithe.

What does Brannoc do?

I'll go, but only to scout. "Wick, Gorm, we pole to the south tip, look from the water, and turn back at the first sign of the lights moving. Nobody lands after four-thirty, and nobody goes near that west door."

I'll bring the rope, the hooded lantern, and a few flasks of oil, and keep Shield of Faith ready. I'll watch the bow-mark and the cut reeds for Jory's skiff or any sign of him. DM: can I see from the water whether Jory's skiff is still tied up at the south tip?

You take the rope, the hooded lantern, and a few flasks, and Wick and Gorm pole the skiff out across the fen. The water is black and slow, and the mist closes behind you. The only sound is the knock of the poles and the hiss of the reeds. You keep the lantern hooded and your voice low, and Wick takes you by the old cutters' channels in a long curve.

At the south tip, about forty paces off, Wick eases the skiff to a stop in the reed-lee and holds her. The Isle is a low grey shape in the mist. You look hard for Jory's skiff, and your Perception is a natural 1, a 4 in all. The mist lies thick on the water and the reeds are crowded and grey. You can't make out the shore at all. There might be a skiff tied up on that raw cut or there might not, and you can't swear which. Wick says quietly that the mark in the mud was fresh a week ago. Gorm says nothing and grips his pole.

The Wick-fires do not move. All three hold steady over the west side, pale and low and silent, and the cold that rolls off the Isle is a damp, unhealthy cold. A reed-cutter's nerve is thin here. When the light begins to fade you keep your word, call the turn, and don't land. You are back at the staithe by twenty past five, with the sun gone orange and the village chimneys lit.

You know the Isle's shape now, the cut reeds, the gap on the west, and the three lights, and not whether Jory is alive. You have four 1st-level slots, no 2nd-level slots, and Channel Divinity. You can't rest again until tomorrow, at the earliest a quarter past three in the afternoon. Ode meets you at the landing, her pole-hook in her hand.

What does Brannoc do?

I step onto the staithe and tell Ode honestly, "I couldn't see Jory's skiff through the mist, Goodwife, so I can't say if he's alive. I kept to my word and didn't land, but we know the way now: the cut reeds on the south tip, the dark gap on the west, and three lights holding steady."

"We go at first light tomorrow, with a full rest behind me. Wick, Gorm, and I will land at the south tip in daylight with rope and oil, and I'll look for Jory before anyone goes near that west door. Tonight I'd like the village fires kept high and someone watching the lights." DM: when will my 2nd-level slots come back, and can Wick and Gorm both stay on the skiff while I land?

Your slots first, and it's an answer you won't like. Your 2nd-level slots come back only when you finish a long rest, and the rules allow only one in 24 hours. Your last one finished at half past three this afternoon, so the next can finish no earlier than half past three tomorrow afternoon. A night's sleep tonight, ending near dawn, won't restore them, though your hit points and 1st-level slots are full already.

That leaves you two honest choices. You can land at first light tomorrow with four 1st-level slots, Channel Divinity, and no 2nd-level slots. That means no Lesser Restoration if the dead mound's chill takes anyone, and no Spiritual Weapon. Or you can start a long rest at half past seven tomorrow, finish at half past three in the afternoon with everything restored, and land around half past four with about an hour of light left. The cost of waiting is a night and a day more for Jory, if he lives, and a daylight window that is shorter than you'd like.

Yes, Wick and Gorm can both stay with the skiff while you land. They'd rather, in truth. Wick grips his pole and says he'll keep her off the reeds and ready to run, and Gorm nods, relieved.

Ode takes your honest report with a grim nod. She does not blame you for turning back, and she will keep the village fires high and a watcher at the landing. Down the walks the lamps come on one by one. Marta brings you a bowl of eel stew and sits with you on the staithe a moment without speaking. The three pale glows hang over the west side of the Isle in the dusk.

It's twenty to six on Day 14. You have four 1st-level slots, no 2nd-level slots, and Channel Divinity.

What does Brannoc do?

I eat Marta's stew and think it over. "Ode, a night is a long time for Jory, but going in without my best prayers is how I end up unconscious on a dead man's doorstep. I'll sleep tonight and land at first light with what I have, and I'll stay on the south tip and shout for him before anything else."

I'll keep Sanctuary and Healing Word ready for Jory, and the rope tied off to the skiff so Wick and Gorm can haul me out. DM: can I ask Ode what Jory's skiff looks like and whether he had a whistle or a horn, so I know what to listen for?

For a long breath there is only dripping. Then one thin bone-note comes back from the west, a single blast, weaker than the three before. Wick whispers, "That's him. That's his whistle."

You kneel at the trail. Survival (21): the prints belong to one person, a young man in cut-down boots. The left foot drags a little at the toe. Two sets of prints overlap, one going out and one coming back, and the coming-back set is the shorter, stumbling stride of someone hurt or exhausted. They run west along the shore, keeping to the trampled reeds, and every one of them bends toward the dark gap. You see no other tracks, bare or booted, and no drag-marks.

The reeds along the trail are grey and brittle, drained of colour. The cold is stronger here, and the air has a faint grave-earth smell. The three pale Wick-fires hang over the west side, still and silent.

RULE Combat Step by Step:
1.  **Determine surprise.** The GM determines whether anyone involved in the combat encounter is surprised.
2.  **Establish positions.** The GM decides where all the characters and monsters are located. Given the adventurers' marching order or their stated positions in the room or other location, the GM figures out where the adversaries are/how far away and in what direction.
3.  **Roll initiative.** Everyone involved in the combat encounter rolls initiative, determining the order of combatants' turns.
4.  **Take turns.** Each participant in the battle takes a turn in initiative order.
5.  **Begin the next round.** When everyone involved in the combat has had a turn, the round ends. Repeat step 4 until the fighting stops.

The rules sections these steps name, in full:

RULE Surprise:
A band of adventurers sneaks up on a bandit camp, springing from the trees to attack them. A gelatinous cube glides down a dungeon passage, unnoticed by the adventurers until the cube engulfs one of them. In these situations, one side of the battle gains surprise over the other.

The GM determines who might be surprised. If neither side tries to be stealthy, they automatically notice each other. Otherwise, the GM compares the Dexterity (Stealth) checks of anyone hiding with the passive Wisdom (Perception) score of each creature on the opposing side. Any character or monster that doesn't notice a threat is surprised at the start of the encounter.

If you're surprised, you can't move or take an action on your first turn of the combat, and you can't take a reaction until that turn ends. A member of a group can be surprised even if the other members aren't.

RULE The Order of Combat:
A typical combat encounter is a clash between two sides, a flurry of weapon swings, feints, parries, footwork, and spellcasting. The game organizes the chaos of combat into a cycle of rounds and turns. A **round** represents about 6 seconds in the game world. During a round, each participant in a battle takes a **turn**. The order of turns is determined at the beginning of a combat encounter, when everyone rolls initiative. Once everyone has taken a turn, the fight continues to the next round if neither side has defeated the other.

Sections inside it (look each up): Combat Step by Step, Surprise, Initiative, Your Turn, Reactions

RULE Initiative:
Initiative determines the order of turns during combat. When combat starts, every participant makes a Dexterity check to determine their place in the initiative order. The GM makes one roll for an entire group of identical creatures, so each member of the group acts at the same time.

The GM ranks the combatants in order from the one with the highest Dexterity check total to the one with the lowest. This is the order (called the initiative order) in which they act during each round. The initiative order remains the same from round to round.

If a tie occurs, the GM decides the order among tied GM-controlled creatures, and the players decide the order among their tied characters. The GM can decide the order if the tie is between a monster and a player character. Optionally, the GM can have the tied characters and monsters each roll a d20 to determine the order, highest roll going first.

The ward holds, and the lights come at you.

You say the prayer, press the powdered silver and iron to your brow, and walk in under your shield. As you come on, the three Wick-fires drop on you, each trailing a bright, crackling tail. Each lashes out with a stinging arc of pale lightning, and each one misses. It slides off the shield, jerks aside, or curdles against the ward. The air smells of hot metal and grave-earth.

These are will-o'-wisps. Each is a tiny dead thing, swift and hard to hit, and each can shock for 9 lightning damage. They can also drink the life out of anyone who falls to 0 HP. They're all around you now, bobbing at shoulder height. Jory lies about twenty feet ahead at the gap's sill, watching with wild eyes.

It's round 2 of the fight. You are unhurt, with two 1st-level slots, Channel Divinity, and Protection from Evil and Good on you. It's a concentration spell, so a hit that hurts you could break it. Your action, your bonus action, and 30 feet of movement are free this turn.

What does Brannoc do?

description.text: Small struggling settlement of farmers and herders on a muddy back road, no priest or healer. Lanterns lit early, doors shut. A barn shelters the sick and wounded.

Day 2 night: Brannoc (now level 2) and Pell and Dorrin Harrow walked the Reach lighting lanterns at every porch; the Long Cut is sealed and ringed with lamps; the village's doors stood open for the first time in days. Brannoc sits his long rest beside Wil in the Harrow barn.

Day 3, 8 AM: Brannoc finished a long rest in the Harrow barn beside Wil; the scratching under the Long Cut did not change in the night. He has Protection from Evil and Good prepared but needs powdered silver and iron (holy water or powder) to cast it.
Boy of about ten from Hollow Reach, mud to the knees, who flags Brannoc down and begs him to come to the Harrow barn.
Large barn at the edge of Hollow Reach, belonging to Widow Harrow. Shelters the wounded after last night's attack from the woods.
Tam's father, big farmer with a torn, bound thigh; gray-faced from blood loss but stoic, asks Brannoc to see to others first.
Gaunt woman in a stained apron who owns the Harrow barn and leads its defence with a hay fork. Her sons are among the wounded.
Old villager of Hollow Reach with broken ribs from the creature's attack; healed by Brannoc's Cure Wounds.

Sons of Widow Harrow, all wounded: Wil (about 14, unclean bite on shoulder, swelling and heat spreading), Pell (deep arm gash, exhausted, asleep), Dorrin (the lantern-carrier at the morning attack, cold, damp, barely waking; Brannoc healed him).
Day 2 ~8:45 AM: Brannoc, rested with prayers back, cast Cure Wounds on Wil first; fever breaking. Pell and Joss still need tending.

Upright, silent figure that attacked Hollow Reach on two nights, takes lanterns, stands at the fence and watches. Gaunt, long-limbed, wrapped in rags, face turned toward the barn's light. Nature not yet revealed; DM to decide (undead or similar SRD creature).
Turn 11: walked to the barn door and stopped, lifting the unlit lantern toward it. Wears a keeper's rags; may be Hob Marrow himself. Has not yet attacked this night.

Turn 12: answered Brannoc through the door in fragments. It is Hob Marrow's remnant, bound by duty to the lamp. Says the lamp was put out, the 'hungry ones' come when it is dark, and he cannot rest without it lit. Unlit lantern is his; he took others trying to relight the way. The wounds on villagers came from other creatures (hungry ones), not from him.
Turn 13: Hob says he never harmed anyone; the hungry ones number about four, tall, come up from under the shrine stones in the dark and range out at night. They did the wounding.
Turn 14: the hungry ones are ghouls (SRD stat block). Hob walks with Brannoc and Cal Tarn to the Lamp, carrying his pale-lit unlit lantern; senses ghouls nearby.

Old wayside shrine in the woods north of Hollow Reach, a stone lamp-house where a keeper kept a light burning for travellers. Keeper was Old Hob Marrow, who has not been seen since harvest; the lamp has been dark since. Villagers avoid it. Possible origin of the Silent Watcher.
Turn 12: per Hob's remnant, the lamp was put out and the 'hungry ones' come when it is dark; relighting it keeps them away. Needs investigating.

Turn 15: two ghouls feed outside the open lamp-house door on a dead pack-pony. Per Hob, the other two ghouls are away roaming (toward the village side). Brannoc, Cal and Hob are about 50 feet off in the trees, unnoticed.

Turn 18: Hob lit the lamp from the pony's pack oil while Ghoul 2 stood over the fallen. DM ruling: the lamp's flame is a hallowed light the ghouls cannot abide; they flee below the flagstone. Ghoul 1 dead. Ghoul 2 fled (19/22 HP). Two other ghouls still roam. Brannoc is stable, wakes ~4 hours later at 1 HP.

Turn 19: Hob says the lamp will burn until dawn on the oil in it, but it needs refilling and tending; he must stay bound to it. Under the stones is an old barrow-crypt whose other mouth opens somewhere toward the village side; the two roaming ghouls may have come up that way. Hob cannot leave the lamp's light for long.

REWIND (player's choice): Brannoc took the full long rest at the lamp, midnight to 8 AM Day 2. Two ghouls roamed; none came to the lamp. At first gray two villagers with a handcart (Dobb Harrow, Widow Harrow's brother-in-law, and a neighbour) came and bore Cal home; they told Hob that Wil's fever is worse but the barn held through the night. Brannoc wakes at full HP and prayers.
Hermit keeper of the Wayfarers' Lamp; vanished around harvest, never found. Villagers say he never missed lighting the lamp, and the lamp has been dark since. Fate unknown.

Day 3: has a sister, Maud Marrow, in Greywater a day down the valley. Hollow Reach proposes a rota to share the Lamp's tending (Pell and Dorrin Harrow with an older hand, oil and candles from the Reach).

Day 3 ~12:15 PM: Brannoc told Hob of the rota and of going to Maud. Hob's message for Maud: tell her he kept the light, that he was not afraid at the end, and that the blue shawl she wove him is in the lamp-house chest (she is to have it back). Lamp-house has a chest with spare wicks and a flint; oil is the real need, candles only a spare.

Day 7 ~2:30 PM: Brannoc hung Maud's blue skein in the lamp-house and told Hob she is coming early next week. Hob says, in the quiet of the night, he hears the crypt beneath the lamp is empty now; the ghouls have gone south along the Dead Road toward the river-town (Stonebridge). Two had already gone before the Drowned Stair fight.

Hob cannot count the ghouls or say where the Dead Road surfaces; he feels footfalls, not numbers. He senses one that moved slowly and dragged a leg (the wounded Ghoul 2, 3 HP). He wants a message sent through Ansel if the stones stir.
The bowman guarding the Harrow barn; a young hunter who knows the north track to the Wayfarers' Lamp well.
DIED at the Wayfarers' Lamp, Day 1 ~8 PM, clawed down by Ghoul 2 after killing Ghoul 1 with Brannoc's oil plan. Hob could not stabilise him.

Four ghouls ("hungry ones") that crawl out from under the Wayfarers' Lamp's flagstone when the lamp is dark. Two are at the lamp-house feeding; two roam toward the village. Fight begins Day 1, ~7:55 PM, as Brannoc's chain mail clinks and they look up.
Round 1: Ghoul 1 crit-clawed Brannoc to 0 HP (he passed the paralysis save). Ghoul 2 clawed Cal Tarn. Cal's lit oil hurt Ghoul 1. Brannoc is dying, 1 death-save success.

Day 2 ~1:30 AM: Brannoc (9 HP, no spells, 20 bolts) meets one of the two roaming ghouls on the track near the Fenner fields. It has heard his armour. The other roams elsewhere. Cal's oil jar burned out in two rounds back at the Lamp.
Day 2 ~1:31 AM: Ghoul 3 (3 HP left) killed Brannoc Ashdown on the track below the Fenner fields. Brannoc died of three death-save failures after two critical claw hits.

Cut bank in the wash below the Fenner fields where the stream undercut an old barrow mound. Old Garrit says the mound is the Hollow Reach folk's 'Old Ones' barrow', older than the village, sealed with fitted stones that the stream has been eating for years. Its mouth opens into the same crypt that lies under the Wayfarers' Lamp. Ghouls' tracks lead into it. Villagers say the barrow roof is thin there; the stones could be dropped with a pry-bar or fire-split wedge. Entrance is about 10 feet wide, scree and roots.

Day 2 ~9:45 AM: Brannoc and Dobb Harrow's crew (four lads from the Reach, with iron bar, sledge, beam, ropes, oil) arrive. Brannoc rolled a natural 1 on Perception; hidden: the north lip of the roof is rotten and will slump if the beam is set there, risking the workers. Ghouls below are quiet by day.

Day 2 ~11:15 AM: Dobb's crew levered the slab; the rotten north lip crumbled, so the collapse covered about four-fifths of the mouth but left a gap ~2 feet wide at the top, north side. Faint scraping heard below as dust settled. Needs filling with rubble/beam/stone and the oil.

Day 2 ~12 PM: oil poured and lit down the gap (burned out in two rounds). Packing with beam and rubble was only half done when a ghoul's hand came up through the gap and seized the beam; Marl is within reach of it. Brannoc has 0 spell slots, full HP, mace, shield, crossbow.

Day 2 ~noon: Ghoul 2 (3/19 HP) killed Marl, Hennet, Dobb Harrow and both Fenner cousins (Wat and Ned) after crawling through the gap; Brannoc fell, stabilised by Hennet's first aid. The ghoul dragged a body down into the barrow and left. The gap is still open, the beam crooked. Brannoc wakes ~2:55 PM at 1 HP, alone, no spell slots until about midnight.

Day 2 ~4 PM: Brannoc prayed over the four bodies left (Ned Fenner's was dragged below), rested an hour, 9 HP. Found Dobb's hooded lantern and a pint of oil in Hennet's satchel. Trail: dark drag-marks and handprints in the dirt from the gap, leading down into the barrow.

Brannoc's plan: seal the second mouth of the barrow at the Long Cut with stone and fire before dark, so the two roaming ghouls (and the one that fled from the Lamp, 19/22 HP) cannot hunt Hollow Reach again. Hob Marrow keeps the lamp lit for the stones' upper mouth. Villagers (Dobb Harrow, Old Garrit, Joss Fenner when able) can help with labour and tools.

Day 2 afternoon: the first attempt failed at heavy cost. Dead: Marl, Hennet, Dobb Harrow, Wat and Ned Fenner. Gap still open. Ghoul 2 is nearly dead (3 HP) and has gone below. Two other ghouls remain. Sealing needs more labour, stone and fire; Joss Fenner and Widow Harrow's folk must be told.

Day 2 ~4:30 PM: Brannoc hauled the four bodies and Cal's longbow home on Dobb's handcart. Lantern with a pint of oil left in the gap (a few hours). Brannoc's 10 candles could stand in the gap but each burns 1 hour. Dusk about 6:30 PM; his next long rest counts around midnight. Needs the village's oil and hands.

Day 2 ~4:40 PM: Brannoc told the village the truth. Hollow Reach agrees to give oil, lanterns and hands; Joss Fenner and Widow Harrow stand with him. Plan needed before dusk (~6:30 PM). No prayers until about midnight.

DONE Day 2 ~6:30 PM: slab dragged by oxen and set over the gap with the whole village's help, just as the sun touched the hills. A finger-wide crack remains at the south corner; the ghouls can scratch but cannot widen it. The barrow is sealed at the Long Cut; Hob keeps the Lamp's mouth lit.
Quick red-haired young villager of Hollow Reach on Dobb's crew. Killed at the Long Cut (Day 2 ~noon) by a ghoul's claws as the beam slid.
Joss Fenner's sister-in-law and mother of Wat and Ned, who died at the Long Cut. Grieving; angry first, then lends oil and hands.
Hob Marrow's younger sister, a weaver in Greywater, a village a day's walk down the valley. Hollow Reach folk assumed Hob had gone to her; no one has told her he is dead.

Day 4 ~9:20 AM: Brannoc reached her blue-door loom-house in Greywater with the shawl and Hob's words. She is a lean, grey-braided woman in her sixties with dyed-blue fingertips, talkative, who guessed from his face before he spoke. Hob had left in spring; they quarrelled about his staying at the Lamp.

Day 6 evening: Plans to take Wren to Stonebridge to Mother Aldith first (a week, when weather holds), then go up to the Lamp after the trip, a few days later than she said. Wants Brannoc to carry up her old loom-stool? No: she asks him to tell the Reach to expect her, and sends a skein of blue wool for Hob's lamp-house.

Day 8 ~3 PM: Told Brannoc the ruined chapel at the ford was the Ford Chapel, abandoned after the Grey Fever years ago; shepherds say sheep vanish near it, and her grandmother called its mound the Sleepers' Hill. She offers her cart-owning cousin and a fortnight's worth of lamp oil from the dye-sheds.

Set up a rota so the Wayfarers' Lamp is tended by living hands as well as Hob: Pell and Dorrin Harrow plus an older villager, oil and candles from Hollow Reach. Also: tell Hob's sister Maud Marrow in Greywater; return Cal Tarn's longbow to his kin.
Day 3 ~11:30 AM: Cal's longbow returned to Nessa Tarn, who will join the Lamp rota in Cal's name. Remaining: carry word of Hob to Maud Marrow in Greywater.
Day 3 ~12:50 PM: Brannoc left five candles at the lamp-house, took Hob's blue shawl and his message for Maud, and set out for Greywater. Millstone Inn is on the way.

Day 4 ~10:45 AM: Brannoc gave Maud the shawl and Hob's words. Maud wept, then said she will come to the Lamp herself within the week with wool and a loom-stool to sit with him; she asks to be told when the Reach's rota begins. All parts of the quest done.
Day 7 ~1 PM: Brannoc returns to Hollow Reach carrying Maud's blue skein and her message (she comes up to the Lamp early next week). Tam meets him on the track. The rota has been running since Day 4.

Cal Tarn's widowed mother, a small, weathered woman who lives at the far end of Hollow Reach's lane. Received Cal's longbow from Brannoc on Day 3 and heard how he died. Will take Cal's place on the Lamp rota with oil and her own hands.

Roadside inn about six hours' walk down the valley road from Hollow Reach, two hours short of Greywater, an old mill converted by a stout widow, Hesper Cole. Clean beds, a common room, stabling. Lodging a few silver; Brannoc may owe a small payment or earn it by tending a sick guest.
Stout, sharp-eyed widow who keeps the Millstone Inn. Blunt, fair, and quick with a ladle. Has a carter's boy ill with a cough in the back room as Brannoc arrives, Day 3 ~7 PM.

Carter's boy of about nine, ill at the Millstone Inn with a chest fever and a wet cough for three days. His father Garn the carter left for Greywater and is due back in two days. Brannoc tended him with Medicine, steam and honey water.

Day 3 night: Brannoc's second Medicine read (13) found a lung fever (settled in the chest, no wound, no magic), not a simple chill. Cooling cloths, propped upright, steam and honey water; by ~1 AM fever eased from its peak. Cure Wounds cannot treat it; Lesser Restoration (level 3 for Brannoc) would end a disease. Garn the carter due back in two days.

Day 4 dawn: fever low, breath easier, sleeping. Brannoc left instructions with Hesper (upright, cool, honey water, send for a healer if his lips go blue) and a note for Garn the carter. Healing Word only restores hit points, so Brannoc did not spend it.
Day 8 ~11:30 AM: sitting up, eating, nearly well; has a weak cough. Calls Brannoc the humming man.

Weaving village in the valley, a day's walk from Hollow Reach and about two hours past the Millstone Inn. Grey slate roofs along a river, racks of dyed wool drying, a small chapel with no resident priest. Maud Marrow's loom-house is at the lower end by the weir, a blue door.

Day 5 dawn: Brannoc slept in the chapel; Osric, Ilsa, Tessa and Perrin tended; Wren taught basic nursing and given a letter for Mother Aldith. Greywater now knows a healer was kind to them. Brannoc heads to Stonebridge.

Girl of about twelve in Greywater, a dyer's daughter who hauls yarn baskets and sweeps the village's priestless chapel. Hopeful and direct. Tells Brannoc the chapel has had no priest since the old one died two winters ago; the sick are tended by the weavers as best they can.

Day 4 afternoon-evening: Brannoc taught Wren to dress a burn, tell fever from chill, and to watch a baby's breathing; she wants to learn more. He will write her a letter for Mother Aldith at Stonebridge asking whether she might take Wren on as an apprentice, but Wren is a dyer's daughter and her parents have not been asked.
Day 5: surname Reed. Her parents Corwin and Hale agreed to a one-month trial with Mother Aldith, with Maud Marrow to travel with her.

Middle-aged weaver of Greywater with a scalded forearm from a dye vat three weeks ago that went red and angry. Brannoc cleaned it, drew the matter with a honey dressing and linen, and judged it will heal without magic if kept clean and changed daily. Taught Wren to change the dressing.

Thin, tired young mother in Greywater with a two-week cough; her baby daughter Tessa (about four months) has the same rattle. Husband Garrick Dunmore is a boatman away upriver hauling dyestuffs, due back in about four days.

Old dyer of Greywater, proud and gruff, who fell from a drying rack a month ago and has walked crooked since; won't let anyone look at it. Brannoc won his trust by asking about the dye work. Injury: left hip and lower back; Brannoc's first read inconclusive (Medicine 8). DM ruling: Cure Wounds restores hit points only and cannot unset an old crooked injury.
Day 4 ~1:50 PM: agreed to a prayer; Cure Wounds eased the ache. Hip still sits crooked. Brannoc showed him a stretch and told him to keep a stool at the vat; recommended Mother Aldith of Stonebridge.
Day 6 afternoon: Has been using the stool at the vat and sleeping through the night since Brannoc's Cure Wounds; privately asking Wren what the priest meant about the bonesetter.
Day 9: Persuaded by Brannoc (20) to ride Tobias's cart to Stonebridge so Mother Aldith can reset his hip. Travels with Maud and Wren. Arrives about 9 PM Day 9.

Bonesetter and midwife at Stonebridge, the market town a day's walk further down the valley beyond Greywater. Known for setting hips and breaking and resetting badly healed bones; charges modest coin. Recommended to Perrin Gale by Brannoc.

Reputation (told to Brannoc Day 4 by Maud Marrow and Perrin Gale): blunt, loud, no patience for fools, and the best bonesetter in the valley; has had three apprentices, two of whom stayed. Wants coin, not charity, from those who can pay, but never turns away the poor. Owes Maud a favour (Maud wove her winter blankets).
Day 5 evening: Brannoc has not yet met her. Her house in Stonebridge is a few streets from the hospice (Ansel can direct him).
Day 6 ~6:30 AM: Brannoc reaches her house on the tanners' lane. Wren kept her original letter, so Brannoc wrote a fresh note in his prayer book for Aldith.

Day 6 morning: Agreed to see Tobin today at the hospice; will read the note on Wren and take her on a trial when she arrives with Maud. Told Brannoc to send Perrin Gale to her only if he comes himself; she won't travel to Greywater before the first frost. She asked Brannoc about the gray marks on Tobin's ankle.

Day 6 ~7:30 AM: At the hospice she set Tobin's ankle; the first set did not quite seat (shy of right), and she grumbles it must be re-done after the swelling eases or the boy will limp. Brannoc told her about the Drowned Stair seal on the walk.

Day 9 evening: Brannoc delivered Perrin Gale, Maud and Wren to her house. She will examine Perrin's hip at dawn and has put Wren on trial. Tobin's ankle reset was done earlier that day by her (swelling down), set properly this time.

Wren's parents, dyers of Greywater (Corwin the father, large and quiet; Hale the mother, quick and careful). After Brannoc's honest account they agreed Wren may go to Stonebridge to meet Mother Aldith with Maud Marrow's company when the weather is fair, for a trial of one month, and that she return at harvest if either wishes. They will keep the chapel swept with her.

Market town a day's walk (about eight hours) down the valley from Greywater, where the valley road crosses the river by a long stone bridge of seven arches. Walled in timber, busy on market days, with a weekly cattle fair, a guildhall, and a small house of the healing faith (a hospice and shrine) run by Brother Ansel. Home to Mother Aldith, the bonesetter.

Grey, cheerful priest who keeps the house of the healing faith at Stonebridge, a hospice of twelve beds beside a plain shrine. Brannoc has a claim on shelter and care there under Shelter of the Faithful. Overworked, short of hands, and eager for another healer.

Morning of Day 5: a carter's cart went over on the seven-arch bridge at Stonebridge. Three hurt: Rudd Fenwick, the carter (shattered thigh, steady bleeding, worst off); Imma, an 11-year-old girl riding with him (head knock, vomiting, drowsy); Tobin, a boy of 9 (ankle crushed, and long gray handprints with cold-burn marks on the ankle, as if grabbed from below). The horse bolted before the cart went over; the carter says something 'pulled the wheel' under the second arch. Brannoc's natural 20 on Medicine noticed the marks: they smell of the same sour grave-air as the Long Cut.

Narrow flight of old river-stairs under the second arch of the Stonebridge bridge, leading down to a flooded stone cellar-vault that predates the bridge. Boatmen avoid it after dark; the bridge-watchman Hodd Pell says lamp-oil goes missing from the arch niches and he hears 'something scratching on the damp stone' at night. Gray handprints found on Tobin's ankle came from below the second arch.

Day 5 ~4:30 PM: per Hodd Pell, water at the stair's foot is about knee-deep in autumn low water. The vault has a grated drain culvert to the river and, by old tale, a sealed 'Dead Road' passage toward the burial hill outside the walls. Seal materials: spare bridge capstones in the quay yard, the iron grating, and oil. Brannoc has Bede buying 50 flasks (about 5 gp) and fetching two more guards, a sledge and an iron bar; lamps hung on poles over the stair. Padlock forced from inside.

Day 5 ~5:50 PM: the crew nearly sealed the grating (capstone and oak wedges) when a ghoul burst up the burning steps; fight began. Two ghouls in the vault (only one fights at first, the other behind it). Guards Bede and Corra are fighting beside Brannoc.
Day 5 ~5:35 PM round 3: Ghoul A at 2 HP clawing through the grating; Bede paralyzed (5 HP) in its reach; Corra 11 HP; Brannoc 16/17 HP with 1 first-level slot left; second ghoul behind in smoke.

Day 5 dusk: two ghouls (A and B) came up the stair and were killed at the grating by Brannoc and the guards Bede and Corra. The grating was then sealed with a capstone, oak wedges and clay. Any further ghouls and the Dead Road passage remain unknown.

Day 9 night: grating, capstone and clay intact, second stone set by Hodd. But the river under the second arch runs unnaturally cold, with a low mist, and a faint scrape of stone is heard from the vault side, not the stair: the drain culvert toward the river is the likely new route. Something is moving in the vault below (a third ghoul, probably the wounded Ghoul 2 or another arrived by the Dead Road).

Day 9 ~10:20 PM: The culvert outlet is a stone-lipped arch-mouth in the quay wall on the east bank, about forty paces downstream of the second arch, a hand's height above the low water, grated with iron bars two fingers apart. A flat bank ledge ten feet above it gives a clear line down. Brannoc brings Corra and Bede.

Day 9 ~10:25 PM: Ghoul C (the wounded ghoul, 3 HP) tried the culvert bars at the east quay and fled up the culvert from burning oil thrown by Brannoc. It is still alive and hurt, and now knows the culvert is watched. Brannoc has Shield of Faith up (10 min).

Bridge-watchman of Stonebridge, a lean, stooped man in his fifties who keeps the bridge lamps and collects the toll. Has noticed lamp-oil missing from the arch niches for a month and scratching under the second arch at night. The stair door is an old iron-banded grating, padlock rusted through.

Captain of the Stonebridge watch, a sharp, scarred woman of forty with a limp, who commands twelve guards. Lent two guards (Bede and Corra) to Brannoc and Hodd for the bridge inspection. Sceptical but fair.

The valley south of Stonebridge is unwalked. Brannoc has not yet heard of a village without a healer there; Ansel or Captain Voss could point to one. Ghoul nests (Long Cut, Drowned Stair) hint at a connected barrow network, the Dead Road, running beneath the valley.
Day 10: Captain Voss names Reedholm, a fen village two days south, with a marsh-fever and no healer. Strong hook for the next errand.

Carter, Piper's father. Reached Greywater on Day 4 and went home to the Millstone Inn on Day 5 after Hesper's message and Brannoc's note. Grateful to Brannoc for sitting with his son; brought word to Greywater that Piper is mending. Rough and plain-spoken.

Old Garrit's name (his grandmother's tale) for a string of old barrow mounds along the valley, said to be joined by one long road under the hills: the Dead Road. Known or suspected links: the Wayfarers' Lamp crypt, the Long Cut, the burial hill outside Stonebridge's walls, and the Drowned Stair vault. Garrit says there were seven; he can name only the Long Cut and the Lamp, and has heard that one lies on the hill above Stonebridge and another near the old ruined chapel on the valley road between the Millstone Inn and Greywater.

Day 12: the Hollow Isle (a drowned barrow in the fen near Reedholm, where reed-cutters fell sick) may be another link; Garrit said seven mounds. Brannoc now knows: Wayfarers' Lamp, Long Cut, Ford Chapel, Stonebridge burial hill (and the Drowned Stair vault). Hollow Isle would be a fifth mound; two more unknown.

Roofless old chapel on the valley road about an hour south of the Millstone Inn, just past a ford. Behind it, hidden by brambles, is a low barrow mound, one of the Sleepers' Chain. Hidden truth: a fallen altar-slab inside covers a stair to a crypt, and the slab has been shifted a hand's width from below; faint gray finger-marks on its underside edge and a few gnawed sheep bones in the nettles by the east wall. The wounded ghoul (Ghoul 2) has not yet come this far. Brannoc failed to spot these from the ford (Perception 9).

Day 8 ~1:40 PM: Brannoc searched up close (Perception 17) and found the shifted altar-slab, the finger-marks and the gnawed bones. He chose not to open it alone; plans to bring Greywater folk and oil to seal it.

Day 9 morning: Brannoc, Corwin, Osric, Tobias and apprentice Fenn sealed the slab with oil, clay, wedges and the mule (first attempt failed by a hair; a second attempt after an hour's rework held). Nothing stirred below. Brannoc earned 100 XP, reaching 900.

Grassy burial hill outside the north wall of Stonebridge, an old barrow, one of the Sleepers' Chain, used for the town's plague dead during the Grey Fever, hence unvisited. Captain Voss's grandmother called it Stair-Wife's Hill. On the east flank, behind an overgrown stone kerb, a low door-slab has been shoved ajar a forearm's width from within; fresh drag-marks run to the culvert side of the hill. The Dead Road reaches the surface here.
Day 10 ~8:50 AM: Ghoul C (last known ghoul of the Sleepers' Chain's Reach/Stair band) died at the east door-slab to Sacred Flame and Bede's halberd. Door slab not yet sealed.

Fen-edge village about two days' walk south of Stonebridge on the river road, reed-cutters and eel-trappers, no healer since old Mother Vane died last spring. Captain Voss says carters bring word of a marsh-fever there and of lights seen over a drowned barrow in the reeds. Not yet visited.

Day 10 evening: carters at the Stonebridge quay say the river road south forks at a wooden milestone (the Eel Fork); the east branch goes to Reedholm along a causeway, two days on foot, with a ferry-rope at the Black Ford. The lights over the drowned barrow are pale green-white and seen on moonless nights, the reed-cutters call them the Wick-fires. A boy named Sedge brought the first fever cases to the Stonebridge market last week and went home sick.

Day 11 night, from Marta Quill: about sixty folk; some fifteen sick, three dead (old Hobb Sallow, a baby, and a reed-cutter named Tam Rush). The sick are those who cut reeds at the Hollow Isle, a low drowned barrow in the fen cut for thatch two weeks ago after the autumn gale stripped roofs. Dab (Marta's son, age five) has a mild fever and is with her sister Wenna. The village is run by Headwoman Ode Rush; no one has tried to cross to the Isle since the Wick-fires appeared.

Day 13 noon: Ode Rush distrustful (Brannoc's Persuasion 4), allows him in under watch of two reed-cutters (Gorm and Wick Hale). Triage (Medicine 15): 18 sick in the fever-house (Ode's great hall on stilts, the 'Long House'). Worst: Sedge (13, near death, delirious), Gammer Hild Pike (old, failing), Wenna Quill? no, Wenna is nursing Dab and is well. Others weaker. Contagion spreads through household bedding made of cut Isle reeds; the cut reeds still lie stacked as thatch on half the roofs. A faint stale-grave smell hangs on the bundles.
Boy of about thirteen from Reedholm who carried eels to Stonebridge market and brought the first marsh-fever cases there; went home sick. Brannoc should ask for him first on arrival. Not yet met.

Empty shepherd's hut a hundred paces off the Eel Fork, roof sound, hearth working. Hidden: a sweat-stained pallet pushed under the bench where a fever-sick traveller (a Reedholm woman, Marta Quill, trying to reach Stonebridge) rested days ago and moved on or collapsed in the reeds; Brannoc's Perception 7 missed it. Faint green-white glimmer low over the reeds at night, unclear to him (Perception 11).

Reed-cutter's wife of about thirty from Reedholm, fever-sick, who set out two nights ago to reach Stonebridge for a healer for her small son Dab (left with kin). Staggers up the causeway with a failing lantern around 10:15 PM Day 11 and reaches the hut. Has the marsh-fever (hot, shivering, delirious in bursts). Carries news: the Wick-fires started when the reeds were cut near the drowned barrow, and the sick are those who cut reeds there.

Day 11 ~10:30 PM: Reached the hut and was looked over by Brannoc (Medicine 19). Living, casts a shadow, no frost-burn. Marsh-fever: hot, shivering, dry cough, cracked lips, a rash of small red spots at the wrists, dark urine; a true disease. Her fever is high but she is lucid enough to speak. Her pallet was under the bench of the hut from two nights ago (she slept here once, then went on to Stonebridge, was turned back at the ford by a flooded stretch and returned).
Day 11 ~midnight: Cured of the fever by Lesser Restoration (2nd-level slot). Weak, hungry, thankful. Plans to return with Brannoc. Sister: Wenna; son: Dab.

Crossing on the Reedholm causeway where a slow black channel cuts the road; a ferry-rope and flat punt kept by a boy named Pim Tarr (about ten), who lives in a lean-to on the near bank. Half a day short of Reedholm. Reach by evening Day 12.

Ten-year-old ferry boy at the Black Ford, whittler, brisk and a little afraid. Orphaned; lives in a reed lean-to by the punt. Says: eighteen sick now in Reedholm; three nights ago he saw Ode Rush's nephew Jory Rush row a skiff toward the Hollow Isle at dusk and not return; the Wick-fires have burned brighter since.

Day 12 night: Jory's skiff left from Reedholm's north landing (the Rush staithe), headed west-northwest across open water to the Isle, about a mile off. The lights drifted nearer: first by the Isle's south tip, now by its west side, toward the village channel. Ode Rush has sent only Sedge and Marta to Stonebridge; no one else has gone for help. Sedge reached Reedholm again sick; Pim has not seen him since.

Headwoman of Reedholm, about fifty-five, broad, weathered, with a reed-cutter's scarred hands and a flat voice. Proud, practical, and frightened beneath it. Her nephew Jory is missing since crossing to the Hollow Isle; her husband Tam Rush died of the fever. She forbids crossing to the Isle and has told no one outside. Will test Brannoc before trusting him.

Day 14 dawn: Brannoc cured Sedge and Hild Pike with Lesser Restoration; Ode saw Sedge's fever break and now trusts him. Reed bundles burned on a mud-flat away from the village; water boiled. No more deaths overnight. She asks him to find Jory but will not give permission to go to the Isle by night.
Day 14 evening: Heard Brannoc's honest report. Agrees to keep village fires high and a watcher at the landing. Wick and Gorm Hale will crew the skiff and stay aboard if he lands.

Nineteen-year-old nephew of Ode Rush, a reed-cutter. Sure the Wick-fires were marsh-gas; crossed to the Hollow Isle alone by skiff on Day 9 dusk with a lantern, a rope, two eel-spears and candle-stubs, to fetch back the cutters' lost knives and a bundle of tools left on the Isle, and to prove the lights harmless. Never returned. Fate unknown.

Day 15 first light: Jory's skiff (tarred green, blue eel painted on the bow, the Rush mark) is beached in the cut reeds at the Isle's south tip. He carried a bone whistle on a cord. Wick Hale heard three short thin blasts from the west side near dawn: a signal of life. Brannoc's own Perception failed (11).

Day 15 dawn: bone whistle sounded three times from the Isle's west; trail of one person's prints (his boots, one dragging foot) leads from his skiff west along the shore toward the dark gap. Answered Brannoc's call with one whistle blast, faint, from the west.

Low reed-fringed island about a mile west-northwest of Reedholm's landing, a drowned barrow mound of the Sleepers' Chain. A grassy hump about forty paces long, ringed by thick reeds, with a fallen standing stone at its west end and a dark gap in the mound's flank facing west. The reeds cut there two weeks ago released a grave-sickness (the fever). Wick-fires (pale green-white will-o-wisp-like glows) drift over the west side. Jory Rush landed on the south tip. Hidden truth: a lesser undead presence, a drowned-barrow wight-spirit that rouses when its cover of reeds is cut, feeds on warmth and the sick; and Jory is alive in the mound's first chamber, hurt and feverish.

Day 14 ~4:40 PM: Brannoc scouted the south tip from the skiff with Wick and Gorm Hale. Perception was a natural 1: mist and reeds hid the shore; he could not tell if Jory's skiff is there. The Wick-fires held steady on the west side. They turned back at dusk.

story.text:
STORY SO FAR (start of game to end of turn 49)

SYSTEM/RULES NOTES I SET UP
- Brannoc Ashdown, human Life cleric, now level 2: HP 17 max, AC 18, 3 first-level slots, Channel Divinity 1/rest. Prepared: Healing Word, Shield of Faith, Guiding Bolt, Sanctuary, Protection from Evil and Good, plus always-prepared Bless and Cure Wounds. Cantrips: Sacred Flame, Guidance, Spare the Dying. Healing spells get +3 from Disciple of Life at 1st level (Cure Wounds is 1d8+6; Healing Word is 1d4+6).
- Lesser Restoration is a 2nd-level spell and a Life domain spell at cleric level 3 (always prepared then). He needs 900 XP for level 3.
- Protection from Evil and Good needs a consumed material component (holy water or powdered silver and iron). Brannoc made a pouch of powdered silver and iron (enough for 3 castings) from Joss Fenner's file filings and Widow Harrow's silver thimble.
- Rulings I made: named allied NPCs at 0 HP make death saves; Cure Wounds does not fix old crooked injuries or diseases; Healing Word cannot treat fever; Preserve Life only heals to half max HP. Command does nothing to undead (ghouls are undead). A leveled bonus-action spell blocks another leveled spell on the same turn.
- Ghoul: AC 12, 22 HP, Bite +2 (2d6+2), Claws +4 (2d4+2, DC 10 CON save or paralysed 1 minute, repeat save at end of each turn). I rolled many natural 20s with ghouls.
- House rules: natural 20 on an ability check gives a bonus discovery/benefit; fixed-HP level-ups; the PC's HP lives on the sheet.

TIMELINE
Day 1, 6:30 PM: Brannoc arrives at Hollow Reach, a small farming settlement with no healer. Boy Tam (about 10) leads him to the Harrow barn, run by Widow Harrow. About 15 people shelter there. Wounded, with names: Joss Fenner (Tam's father, torn thigh), Wil Harrow (14, unclean bite on shoulder, spreading fever), Pell Harrow (arm gash), Dorrin Harrow (cold, barely waking), Old Garrit (broken ribs). Brannoc did Medicine triage (17), cast Cure Wounds on Garrit (13) and Dorrin (8), spending both slots. Bowman Cal Tarn guarded the barn with another man.
A tall gaunt rag-wrapped figure with an unlit lantern came to the barn door and rasped "...light." It was the dead keeper Hob Marrow, who was keeper of the Wayfarers' Lamp (a stone lamp-house in the beechwoods a mile north). Hob vanished around the harvest; the lamp was put out. He is a speaking undead remnant bound to the lamp's light, not hostile. He took lanterns only to try to relight the lamp. The "hungry ones" are four ghouls that come up from a barrow-crypt under the lamp-house when the lamp is dark; they did the wounding. Hob said two ghouls are out roaming and two stay at the lamp.
Brannoc cleaned and bound Wil's bite (Medicine 22) and set out with Cal and Hob carrying a quart of lamp oil.
Fight at the Lamp: Brannoc's armour clinked (Stealth 4). Cal threw the lit oil jar on Ghoul 1. Ghoul 1 crit-clawed Brannoc to 0 HP. Cal killed Ghoul 1 but was clawed down by Ghoul 2 and died. Brannoc stabilised on his own (three death-save successes). Hob lit the lamp from the pony's oil, and Ghoul 2 (19/22 HP) fled back under the flagstone. Brannoc got 200 XP.
Brannoc woke at 11:55 PM at 1 HP.

THE REWIND (player's choice): In the first timeline Brannoc did a short rest, walked south at 1 AM, and was killed by Ghoul 3 on the track. The player asked to replay from waking at the lamp with a full long rest instead. That death never happened in the story now. Only the replay timeline counts. Ghoul 3 never fought Brannoc.

REPLAY TIMELINE
Night of Day 1 into Day 2: Brannoc took a long rest at the lamp-house under Hob's watch (midnight to 8 AM). At first gray, Dobb Harrow (Widow Harrow's brother-in-law) and a neighbour came with a handcart and took Cal's body home. They left Cal's longbow for Brannoc.
Day 2, 8 AM: Hob stays at the lamp. Brannoc walked to the barn and cast Cure Wounds on Wil (11, fever breaking) and Pell (14). Old Garrit and Joss said the Long Cut is an old barrow mound in the wash below the Fenner fields. Its roof is thin and the stream undercut it. Its south mouth opens into the same crypt as under the Lamp. Brannoc planned to seal it.
Day 2, about 9:45 AM to noon: Dobb Harrow led a crew: Hennet, Marl, and two Fenner cousins, Wat and Ned. They levered the roof slab (Athletics 13, with Brannoc's natural 1 on Perception). The north lip crumbled, leaving a 2-foot gap. Oil poured and lit down the gap bought time. A ghoul (Ghoul 2) then reached up through the gap and killed Marl, Hennet, Dobb, Wat and Ned. Ned's body was dragged below. Brannoc fell to 0 HP. Hennet stabilised him with first aid before dying. Ghoul 2 went below at 3 HP.
Brannoc woke at 2:55 PM with 1 HP. After a short rest (Hit Die spent) he had 9 HP. He prayed over the four bodies, put Dobb's lantern with a pint of oil in the gap, and hauled the bodies home on the handcart.
Day 2, about 4:30 PM: He told the village the truth. Berra Fenner (mother of Wat and Ned, Joss's sister-in-law) was bitterly angry, then gave oil. Widow Harrow and Joss backed him. The whole village used oxen to drag a slab over the gap by dusk (Athletics 11 with advantage). It left a finger-wide crack at the south corner; scratching continues but can't widen it. The Long Cut quest is done (+100 XP). He reached level 2 (300 XP) and took 7 HP fixed.
Day 2 night: He and Pell and Dorrin lit lanterns at every porch. He prepared Protection from Evil and Good as his fifth spell, after dropping Command (no effect on undead) and learning Lesser Restoration was not yet available. Long rest from midnight to 8 AM Day 3.
Day 3 morning: Brannoc made the powder. At a village meeting, a rota for tending the Lamp was agreed: Pell and Dorrin will watch with an older hand, Old Garrit will walk the track by day, and Berra Fenner will send oil weekly. Brannoc returned Cal's longbow to Cal's mother Nessa Tarn (small weathered woman, lives at the lane's far end), sat two hours with her, and gave her the words of Edda's hymn. She will join the rota in Cal's name.
Day 3, about 12 PM: At the Lamp, Hob gave Brannoc his message for his sister Maud Marrow, a weaver in Greywater, a day down the valley. The words are: "Tell her I kept the light. Tell her I was not afraid, at the end. There is a shawl, blue. She wove it the winter I came here. She is to have it back. Tell her it was warm, every night. She talks too much. She will say I should have come home. Tell her I had somewhere to be." Brannoc took the blue shawl from the lamp-house chest and left 5 of his 10 candles on the step. The lamp is full; oil is the real need.
Day 3, 12:50 PM: He set out down the valley road. At 6:50 PM he reached the Millstone Inn, a converted mill two hours short of Greywater. Hesper Cole, the stout widow who keeps it, greeted him and asked him to look at a sick carter's boy, with bed and supper free either way. This is where turn 49 ends. (Turn 50 onward, preserved verbatim, covers Piper's illness, the night vigil, and what follows.)

STATE AT END OF TURN 49 (Day 3, 6:50 PM)
- Brannoc: HP 17/17, AC 18, 3/3 first-level slots, Channel Divinity ready, both Hit Dice, XP 300/900, level 2. 15 gp. Items include shield, mace, chain mail, light crossbow and 20 bolts, 5 candles, tinderbox, 2 rations, waterskin, alms box, incense, censer, vestments, amulets, prayer book, powder pouch, blue shawl.
- Everyone from the Reach's wounded is healed except Joss (mending, limping on a crutch). Five villagers and Cal are dead. The Long Cut is sealed, with Ghoul 2 (3 HP) and two other ghouls still below. Hob keeps the Lamp lit. No Fenner or Harrow family member is angry with Brannoc now, though Berra grieves.
- NPC knowledge/wants: Hob wants his sister told and the light kept. Maud does not yet know Hob is dead. The Reach folk want the Lamp tended. Tam adores Brannoc and asked him to come back; Brannoc made no promise. Nessa Tarn has the bow.
- Open quests: Lamp Watch (mostly set up; remaining is telling Maud and the hospice errands), and the notebook has all NPCs (Tam, Joss Fenner, Widow Harrow, Cal, Hob, Nessa, Berra, Garrit, the Harrow brothers, Marl, Hesper Cole, Piper, The Millstone Inn, Greywater, Maud Marrow, Stonebridge, Brother Ansel, Mother Aldith etc.). Greywater and later places were already sketched.
- Decisions I've made that haven't come out in play: Greywater has Wren (dyer's daughter, about 12, sweeps the priestless chapel), her parents Corwin and Hale Reed, Osric (scalded arm), Ilsa Dunmore and baby Tessa, Perrin Gale (crooked hip). Stonebridge, a day further down the valley, has Brother Ansel's twelve-bed hospice, Mother Aldith the bonesetter (blunt, owes Maud a favour), and a ghoul nest at the Drowned Stair under the second bridge arch. Ghouls from the barrow-crypt network may connect beneath the valley (the Dead Road passage). Hob's remnant is bound to the lamp's light.

STORY SO FAR (start of game to end of turn 101)

RULES AND RULINGS I SET UP
- Brannoc Ashdown, human Life cleric. He is now level 3: max HP 24, AC 18 (chain mail + shield), 4 first-level slots and 2 second-level slots, Channel Divinity 1/rest, Preserve Life 15 HP. Always prepared: Bless, Cure Wounds, Lesser Restoration, Spiritual Weapon. He prepares 6 more after a long rest. Current six: Healing Word, Shield of Faith, Guiding Bolt, Sanctuary, Protection from Evil and Good, Command. Cantrips: Sacred Flame, Guidance, Spare the Dying. Healing spells get +3 from Disciple of Life at 1st level, so Cure Wounds is 1d8+6 and Healing Word is 1d4+6. Spell save DC 13, spell attack +5.
- Level 4 needs 2,700 XP. I keep XP on the sheet.
- Prepared spells can only be changed when a long rest finishes. The tool refuses to change them any other way. I once wrongly invited a mid-day change and took it back. Only one long rest counts per 24 hours, and the tool checks the finishing time.
- Detect Poison and Disease needs a yew leaf, which he doesn't carry. He wants it later.
- Protection from Evil and Good consumes powdered silver and iron. The pouch is now enough for 2 castings.
- Other rulings: a bonus-action leveled spell blocks another leveled spell that turn. Cure Wounds does not fix old crooked bones or diseases. Healing Word cannot treat fever. Preserve Life heals only up to half max HP. Command does nothing to undead.
- Lighting a flask of oil from a lantern is a free object interaction (my ruling). Thrown lit oil burns 2 rounds, 5 fire damage to a creature entering or ending its turn there. Cover from a grating gives +2 AC.
- Ghoul stats used: AC 12, 22 HP, Bite +2 (2d6+2), Claws +4 (2d4+2, DC 10 CON save or paralysed 1 minute, repeat at end of each turn). Ghouls are undead.
- House rules: a natural 20 on an ability check gives a bonus discovery. Level-ups use fixed HP (Brannoc took the fixed 7 at level 2 and level 3). Named NPCs at 0 HP make death saves.
- A natural 20 on an attack is a crit.

EARLY STORY (turns 0 to 49, summary)
Day 1, 6:30 PM: Brannoc arrived at Hollow Reach, a small farming settlement with no healer. Boy Tam led him to the Harrow barn, where Widow Harrow shelters about 15 people. The wounded were Joss Fenner (Tam's father, torn thigh), Wil Harrow (bite, fever), Pell Harrow (arm), Dorrin Harrow (cold, barely waking) and Old Garrit (broken ribs). Ghouls from a barrow-crypt under the Wayfarers' Lamp had wounded them. The dead keeper Hob Marrow, a speaking undead bound to the lamp's light, came to the barn door asking for light.

Brannoc, bowman Cal Tarn and Hob went to the Lamp. Cal died there. Brannoc fell to 0 HP and stabilised himself, and Hob relit the lamp. The player then asked for a rewind, so only the replay timeline counts: a long rest at the lamp-

My reply was stopped by a safety classifier, so the story summary you asked for never got written. I'm not going to try that summary again, reworded or otherwise, since I was told not to.

The notebook is untouched. It still has every name, place and fact from play, and the sheet and clock are as the last status showed them. The game itself stopped at turn 121. Brannoc is at the Hollow Isle's south tip at ten past seven on Day 15 with Wick and Gorm in the skiff. Jory's skiff is beached in the cut reeds, and a bone whistle has just sounded three times from the west.

Tell me what Brannoc does next and I'll carry on from there. If you want a record of the story so far, tell me what you'd like it to cover and I'll write that instead.
